title: Localization framework host manifest, schema v1
$doc: This schema is FRAMEWORK-OWNED. The instance it validates is HOST-AUTHORED.
The manifest declares WHAT EXISTS AND HOW IT IS ORGANIZED. It never declares HOW TO
RECOVER THAT FROM BYTES. F2 ADR-2's discriminator governs every field: if changing the
engine from regex to AST — or from a dist/ walk to a build hook — would require editing
the manifest, the manifest has absorbed procedure. A field that survives that change is
structure. `entryStyle`, `collection` and `parser` were all rejected under that test.
Unknown keys are REJECTED, not ignored. A typo'd key that silently does nothing is the
`4h.nonBoundaries` failure (F2 measurement M-4) reproduced in the contract layer. `$doc`
is therefore allowed explicitly wherever prose is useful.
SECTIONS 3-6 ARE OPTIONAL IN v1 BY DESIGN. They are the ratified shape of couplings C-2
and C-4 through C-6, recorded here so the contract is complete and additive changes stay
additive. The host instance declares a section only when a consumer reads it: shipping
config that nothing reads is the same defect as M-4, stated in the other direction.

manifestVersion.$doc: The engine refuses a version it does not know, forward AND backward. A field that changes meaning bumps this; additive optional fields do not.

$doc: The host's own registry is the source of truth for codes; `entries` adds the framework
facts it does not carry. The adapter asserts keys(entries) === codes(registry) and fails
closed on drift. A CHECKED second list is not a second source of truth — the stale 4-of-8
locale list in astro.config.mjs is what an UNCHECKED one looks like.

binding.$doc: Names WHAT THE HOST CALLS its locale registry, not how to find it. Regex to AST does not change the name.

$doc: Names the registry field carrying each locale's text direction. Same class as
`codeField`: WHAT THE HOST CALLS the field, never how to recover it from bytes.
It belongs here and NOT in `entries` because the host registry already carries
direction — `entries` adds only facts it does not carry, and copying this one
would create the second, unchecked source of truth this section exists to avoid.
OPTIONAL, and its absence is a declared fact rather than a default. A host that
does not declare it cannot be asked for direction: the adapter refuses instead of
answering 'ltr', because an invented direction would silently approve an RTL
locale rendering left-to-right — the exact defect gate 4k exists to catch.
Names the registry field carrying each locale's formatting tag — the BCP-47 tag
every machine-formatted date and number renders through (ADR-8: it is a separate
fact from hreflang, and Arabic is where the two diverge). Same class as
`directionField`: WHAT THE HOST CALLS the field, never how to recover it from bytes,
and it points at the registry rather than copying it because `getIntlLocale()` reads
the registry, so gate 4p must read the same fact, not a transcription of it.
OPTIONAL, and its absence is a declared fact rather than a default. A host that does
not declare it cannot be asked which tag formats a locale: the adapter refuses
instead of guessing, because an invented tag would let gate 4p certify a numbering
system the site never renders — the exact silence ADR-8 exists to end.

routes.$doc: OPTIONAL in the instance until the phase that migrates coupling C-2 (the dist/ walk) lands.

dictionaries.$doc: OPTIONAL in the instance until the phase that migrates couplings C-4/C-5 lands.

policy.$doc: OPTIONAL in the instance until the phase that migrates coupling C-3 lands.

structures.$doc: OPTIONAL in the instance until the phase that migrates coupling C-6 (HUB_SLUGS) lands.

$doc: F5 Phase 5 (contract §8.1). ADDITIVE AND OPTIONAL, so manifestVersion stays 1 —
the schema's own drift rule: a field that changes meaning bumps the version, a
field that only adds capability does not. A host with no census section resolves
exactly as it did before this section existed.

doc.$doc: Prose carried in the manifest. Allowed everywhere precisely because unknown keys are rejected.

$doc: F3-B1 is DELIBERATELY NOT RESOLVED BY THIS FIELD. Gate 4g's identity signal needs the
default locale's corpus as its reference set; that is a framework-level truth ('default
locale corpus = reference corpus'), enforced as an engine invariant, not a host fact.
`role` records the host's own view and must not be read as the source of that semantics.
Widening the schema here is the precedent that kills the declarative boundary.

script.$doc: The fine vocabulary subsumes 4h's coarse `cjk`, which is retired. Declared once here; F2 M-1 measured it declared 4x and already drifted.

localePrefix.$doc: The host's URL policy, not a routing algorithm. A build-hook engine would still need it and would not change it.

keyField.$doc: Kept under the discriminator: which field carries permanent identity is a host modelling decision. An array of objects has no canonical key the engine could infer.

requiredFields.$doc: `["*"]` means every canonical key must be present.

policy.$doc: Paths only. Contents stay host-owned — a gate config answers 'how should the framework behave', which is not what this manifest is for.

additionalProperties.$doc: null means the gate has no config file by design (4j).

$doc: WHERE census output lives. Never what a census fact means, and never a fact.
The same rule as `policy`, applied to the other direction of the data flow:
`policy` addresses files a human authors, `census` addresses files a producer
writes. If a locale, a phrase, a count or a threshold ever appears in this
section, the manifest has absorbed census content — revert rather than extend.
F2 ADR-2's discriminator, verbatim: a field that would have to be edited if the
census switched extractors is procedure, not structure.
`facts` is keyed by census KIND, so a host that has produced one kind declares
one entry. A kind declared with no file is not the same as a kind absent: the
first is a broken declaration and fails closed, the second means the host has
never produced that kind, which the consumer is entitled to have an opinion
about ('absence is not a fact', contract §4).
Closed against the kinds census v1 declares. An unknown kind here would be a
file nothing can read, announced as if it were readable — the M-4 defect with
a filename attached.
